PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called meeting to order at 5:02 p.m. in the Council Chambers. 

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on Closed Session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:03 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:26 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items:

Item #1 and #2.B - staff provided presentation, the City Council provided feedback and no reportable action was taken on any of these items.  

City Council did not discuss items #2.A, 2.C, 2.D and 2.E.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:28 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Human Resources Director Pappo led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Councilmember Garcia offered the invocation. 

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Mayra Duarte provided an update for the last two weeks and a presentation on COPS team responsibilities and community policing. 

Discussion took place regarding homelessness, and it was stated that the City utilizes Measure H money to dedicate a number of beds in the Bell Shelter for the homeless. Still, these beds typically do not get used. 
 

2.. Recognition of the Commerce Crush Teams for their 2022 Season Mayor and Councilmembers recognized the Commerce Crash Teas for their successful season.

3.. Certificate of Recognition for Ralph Santana, Nationwide Environmental Services, for his Dedicated Service to the Community and Residents of Commerce Mayor and Councilmembers recognized Ralph Santana, Nationwide Environmental Services, for his service to the community.  Mayor Rebollo added that she received several requests from residents speaking very highly of Mr. Santana and wishing to recognize him for his outstanding service to the community.   



PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing at address the City Council on any items within their jurisdiction. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Councilmember Lainez asked to pull item #5 from the Consent Calendar.  

Vice Mayor Argumedo moved, seconded by Councilmember Altamirano, to approve the Minutes of June 28, 2022.  The motion carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo (4)
Abstained: Councilmember Lainez 

7.. Purchase of One (1) Toyota Electric Forklift Model 05-8FBM25T From Atlas Toyota Material Handling

8.. Award a Construction Contract to CEM Construction Corporation for Design and Installation of Charging Stations for the City’s Electric Buses  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Director of Transportation McFerguson provided an overview of the staff report. 

Discussion took place regarding transitioning the charging station to a new facility. Director McFerguson stated that the new facility would include all specifications and would be a smooth transition. 

Mayor Rebollo asked that staff provide an estimate for dedicating back Dial-A Ride bus back to the Senior Center to avoid all those inconveniences and complaints. 




5.. Approval of Minutes

6.. Re-Ratifying the Proclamation of a State of Emergency by Governor Newsom, and Re-Authorizing Remote Teleconference Meetings of the Legislative Bodies of the City of Commerce for the 30-Day Period

4.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 24A,  24B, 2A and 2B

SCHEDULED MATTERS

9.. Exide Cleanup Activities Update Deputy Director of Operations Nila provided an overview of the staff report. DTSC identified four hundred seventy-one homes as priority properties; up to date, 318 were completed/cleaned up. 

Mayor Rebollo asked staff to arrange a meeting with the DTSC representative to answer all questions related to EXIDE . Discussion took place about landscaping and some complaints that residents had. 
Councilmember Lainez asked whether there are any plans to evaluate the contamination zone.


10.. Amending the Director of Public Works Job Specification  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo City Manager Cisneros provided an overview of the staff report. 

Councilmember Garcia stated that the standards should not be lowered regarding civil engineer registration requirements. Councilmember Garcia moved to keep the requirement or Option 1, and the motion died for the lack of a second. 

City Manager Cisneros recommended option 3, making a requirement Master's Degree or civil engineer registration. Further discussion took place that having more candidates and a bigger pool would allow selecting the most qualified candidate while also interviewing an existing candidate with civil engineer registration. 


ORDINANCES

11.. Adoption and Second Reading of the Ordinance Changing Date of Election to Statewide General Election Date  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk Shumway provided a brief overview of the staff report. 

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmembers and the Mayor thanked all staff involved for National Night Out.

Councilmember Garcia reported that she attended Unplugged performance and Youth Advisory Commission. 

Councilmember Altamirano asked that more patrol is provided as people breaking into cars. Councilmember Altamirano thanked the staff for arranging a tour of La Mirada station. 

Councilmember Lainez invited residents to Back To School this coming Friday. 

Vice Mayor Argumedo recommended that next year's National Night Out include more activities for kids. Vice Mayor Argumedo reported that he attended the Unplugged performance and asked that staff looks to accommodate Veteran's park kids during the transition. Vice Mayor Argumedo thanked for the tour of the La Mirada substation and requested that staff be diligent before the City commits to the substation here and not be left with all expenses and running that facility. 

Mayor Rebollo reported that she attended the Unplugged performance, the library end-of-summer reading program event, and thanked Vice Mayor Argumedo for the backpack event giveaway he recently organized. Mayor Rebollo reminded residents to call 1800-smog if there is any pollution. 



ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:59 p.m.
